page: OVHcloud l4-180 is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance powered by the KVM hypervisor and configured on the x86_64 architecture. Compute is driven by an AMD EPYC 9454 processor providing 45 dedicated physical cores and 45 vCPUs operating at a base clock speed of 2.75 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. Hardware acceleration includes vector and matrix instruction support via AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. System memory totals 180.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio. Bundled hardware resources feature two NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPUs delivering a combined 48 GB of VRAM, 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluation highlights robust execution across multi-core compute and graphical acceleration tasks. In raw CPU execution, stress-ng benchmarks position both single-core and multi-core performance in the top tier, supported by a PassMark CPU score of 75,707.48 and strong Geekbench multi-core results. The dual L4 GPUs demonstrate top-tier throughput for language model inference, reaching 12,232.17 prompt tokens per second on small 135M parameter models and 2,768.53 prompt tokens per second on medium 7B models. Inference for large 70B models remains viable with 262.6 prompt tokens per second and 5.78 generation tokens per second.

The instance delivers high hardware density by pairing 45 dedicated AMD EPYC cores with dual enterprise-grade L4 accelerators, providing high compute efficiency without hyperthreading contention. While memory bandwidth shows top-tier cached throughput, large uncached reads align closer to median cloud tiers. Additionally, the 400 GB NVMe volume offers fast local I/O but requires external object or block solutions for datasets requiring larger capacity. The instance includes 0 complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which requires network planning.

OVHcloud l4-180 is well suited for modern AI workloads, specifically LLM prompt processing, mid-size model inference serving, and image generation pipelines. The combination of dedicated x86_64 execution units and 180 GB of system memory also fits high-concurrency database operations, multi-threaded compilation, and parallel ETL batch jobs.

Graphics and acceleration capabilities are provided by two bundled NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPUs with 48 GB total VRAM. The instance includes 400 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and 16 Gbps baseline network throughput. In benchmark tests, the configuration exhibits top-tier multi-core compute and leading LLM inference speeds across small and medium model sizes. It offers an efficient balance of dedicated host compute and GPU acceleration, making it an effective platform for AI inference pipelines, video processing, multi-threaded software compilation, and high-throughput data processing workflows.
